\section*{Nurture SRG papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG02-P1-PHY-S1-Q01, source={Nurture SRG - Test 02 (06 Dec 2023)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=single, subtopic={Young's modulus}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S3 I2 C2 F0}, diff_note={concepts: elastic energy of a rod partly supported by buoyancy and a force | steps: force balance with buoyancy; tension along the rod; strain energy density; integrate over the length; value}]
A thin uniform elastic rod of natural length $\ell$, area of cross-section $A$, density $\rho$ and Young's modulus $Y$ is just completely immersed in vertical position in fluid of density $2\rho$ by applying a vertically downward force $(F)$ at its top end. The rod is in equilibrium. Elastic deformation energy stored in the rod is (Neglect lateral strain in the rod and the atmospheric pressure)\par
\bfig{121.3}{NSRG02_p1_phy_s1_q01_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{7\rho^2A\ell^3g^2}{6Y}$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{9\rho^2A\ell^3g^2}{8Y}$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{3\rho^2A\ell^3g^2}{4Y}$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{4\rho^2A\ell^3g^2}{3Y}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG02-P1-PHY-S1-Q03, source={Nurture SRG - Test 02 (06 Dec 2023)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Stress and strain}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: stress and energy in a hanging rod | steps: stress along the rod; extension by integration; energy; check options}]
A metal rod of length $\ell$ \& area of cross-section $A$ is suspended to the celling by one of its end. The density of metal is $\rho$, young modulus of elasticity is $Y$. Choose the correct option
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The stress at mid point is $\ell\rho g$}
\opt{B}{Extension in rod due to it's own weight $\Delta\ell=\dfrac{\rho g\ell^2}{2Y}$}
\opt{C}{Potential energy stored in rod due to its own weight $U=\dfrac{\rho^2AL^3}{3Y}$}
\opt{D}{The stress at mid point is $2\ell\rho g$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG02-P1-PHY-S2-Q10, source={Nurture SRG - Test 02 (06 Dec 2023)}, paper=1, qno=10, type=multi, subtopic={Stress and strain}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: metal ring on a cone | steps: force balance of an element; tension from the weight; dependence on radius; energy stored}]
A uniform metallic ring of mass $m$, radius $R$, cross sectional area `a' and Young's modulus $Y$ is kept on a smooth cone of radius $2R$ and semi vertical angle $45^\circ$ as shown. [Assume that extension in the ring is small]\par
\bfig{90.4}{NSRG02_p1_phy_s2_q10_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The tension in the ring is same throughout.}
\opt{B}{The tension in the ring is independent of the radius of the ring.}
\opt{C}{The tension in the ring is $\dfrac{mg}{2\pi}$.}
\opt{D}{Elastic potential energy stored in the ring is $\dfrac{m^2g^2R}{4\pi aY}$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG02-P1-PHY-S2-Q11, source={Nurture SRG - Test 02 (06 Dec 2023)}, paper=1, qno=11, type=multi, subtopic={Stress and strain}, answer={A,B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: stress along a rod with equal forces | steps: force on a section; stress at points; net extension; stored energy}]
A uniform rod of mass $m$ and length $\ell$ is acted upon by two forces each of magnitude $F$ as shown in the figure. The length of the rod is $\ell$, area of cross section is $A$, the young's modulus of the material is $Y$. Select correct alternative(s)\par
\bfig{79.1}{NSRG02_p1_phy_s2_q11_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Stress at the mid point of the rod is zero.}
\opt{B}{Stress at $x=\dfrac\ell4$ is $\dfrac F{2A}$.}
\opt{C}{Net change in length of the rod is zero.}
\opt{D}{Total energy stored in the rod is zero}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG02-P1-PHY-S3-Q05, source={Nurture SRG - Test 02 (06 Dec 2023)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Stress and strain}, answer={2}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: rotating ring and the increase in radius | steps: tension from rotation; stress and strain; increase in radius; value of N}]
A circular ring of radius $R$ \& mass $m$ made by a uniform wire of cross-section area $A$ is rotated about a stationary vertical axis passing through its centre \& perpendicular to the plane of the ring. If young's modulus of material of ring is $Y$ \& increment in radius of ring equals to $\dfrac{mR^2\omega^2}{N\pi AY}$ without breaking find value of $N$. If breaking stress of ring is $\sigma$.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG02-P1-PHY-S3-Q06, source={Nurture SRG - Test 02 (06 Dec 2023)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=numerical, subtopic={Elasticity}, answer={9}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: force needed for wires of equal volume | steps: length from the volume; stiffness of each wire; force ratio; value}]
Two wires are made of the same material and have the same volume. However, wire 1 has cross-sectional area $A$ and wire-2 has cross-sectional area $3A$. If the length of wire 1 increases by $\Delta x$ on applying force 1 newton, how much force is needed to stretch wire 2 by the same amount ?
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S2-Q11, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=11, type=multi, subtopic={Stress and strain}, answer={A,C,D}, answer_src=solved, working={F is slightly more than the elastic force, so the work is $\int\dfrac{YA x}{L}dx=\dfrac{YA\ell^2}{2L}$, stored entirely as elastic energy}, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: work done on a wire stretched slowly | steps: force equals the elastic force; work as an integral; stored energy; energy is not lost}]
A metal wire length $L$, cross section area $A$, and Young's modulus $Y$ is stretched by a variable force $F$. $F$ is varying in such a ways that $F$ is always slightly greater than the elastic forces of resistance in the wire. When the elongation in the wire is $\ell$, up to this instant
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The work done by $F$ is $\dfrac{YA\ell^2}{2L}$}
\opt{B}{The work done by $F$ is $\dfrac{YA\ell^2}{L}$}
\opt{C}{The elastic potential energy stored in wire is $\dfrac{YA\ell^2}{2L}$}
\opt{D}{No energy is lost during elongation}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S3-Q02, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Young's modulus}, answer={11}, answer_src=solved, working={Sag $20$ mm on each half of $0.6$ m: $T=\dfrac{mg}{2\sin\theta}=4.27$ N, extension $=2(\sqrt{0.6^2+0.02^2}-0.6)=6.67\times10^{-4}$ m, so $Y=\dfrac{T/A}{\Delta L/L}=9.8\times10^{11}$ and $x=11$ (the printed key value 13 does not follow)}, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K1 S3 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: Young's modulus of a wire from the sag | steps: geometry of the sag; tension from the load; extension of the wire; stress and strain; exponent}]
A 1.2 m long metal wire is fixed securely at both ends to two solid supports so that the wire is initially horizontal. When a 29 g mass is attached from the midpoint of the wire, the midpoint is observed to move down by 20 mm. If the diameter of the wire is 0.1 mm, the Young's modulus for the wire material is $9.8\times10^x$. Find $x$.
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S1-Q03, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={Stress and strain}, answer={D}, answer_src=solved, working={$U=\dfrac{F^2L_0}{4YA}\left(1+\tfrac12\right)=\dfrac{3F^2L_0}{8AY}$}, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: elastic energy of a bar of two cross sections | steps: extension of each part; energy of each; sum}]
A bar in figure below is made from a single piece of material having Young's modulus $Y$. It consists of two segments of equal length $\dfrac{L_0}2$ and cross-sectional area $A$ and $2A$. The elastic potential energy stored under the action of an axial force $F$ is\par

\opt{B}{$\dfrac{3}{AY}F^2L_0$}
